subject: Post-call: pilot scope & inference cost recap (PivotalPay)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@pivotalpay.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@pivotalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & pilot framing

Alexis / Samir — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a clear next step list.

Key pain points you called out:
- Token/unit cost is a blocker for expanding NLU features beyond highest-value flows. Current spend spikes unpredictably on peak nights.
- High variability in latency (95th percentile) when batching variable-length requests; this drives user-visible degradation.
- Limited engineering bandwidth to maintain a custom inference stack, and concerns about operational coverage during peak season.

Current stack / constraints:
- Production: proprietary BERT-derived reranker + a mix of in-house LLMs for few-shot generation; serving on a mix of AWS g4/g5 instances behind K8s.
- Typical batch sizes: 1–8 for interactive flows; up to 64 for nightly re-ranks.
- Hard latency SLO on interactive flows: <= 350ms at p95.
- Data residency: US-only; some redaction before tokens leave control plane.

Success criteria for a pilot (what good looks like):
1) Clear unit-cost delta vs. your baseline (target: >= 30% reduction in $/generated-token for the targeted flows).
2) Maintain or improve p95 latency for interactive endpoints (<= 350ms).
3) No change to customer-visible behavior for the primary NLU models (quality parity within current thresholds).

What we propose for a 6-week pilot:
- Week 0–1: access + ingestion of 2 production prompt sets (interactive + nightly re-rank).
- Week 2–3: run parallel inference with Redwood-hosted variant (quantization + batching optimizations) and capture token-level cost/latency.
- Week 4: quality validation against your eval prompts and regression thresholds.
- Week 5–6: final readout + cost/ops recommendations and optional rollback plan.

Open questions we agreed to resolve:
- Which specific re-rank workloads should we prioritize for the initial run (interactive vs. nightly)?
- Are you open to trying int8/4-bit quantized variants for model candidates (we can run quality checks first)?
- Clarify peak batch size distribution for autoregressive generation path.

Attachments sent with this email:
- pilot-scope-outline.pdf (high-level timeline + responsibilities)
- redwood-cost-model.csv (example comparative unit-econ)

Next steps (action owners):
- Rafael: share SOC2 summary + pilot SOW draft by Mon 2/22 (attached).
- Alexis: confirm which re-rank workload we should prioritize and provide a sample of nightly batch sizes by Tue 2/23.
- Samir: share procurement timeline & PO contact if pilot approval requires a purchase order.
- Marissa: scheduling technical deep-dive (solutions engineer) pending Alexis availability — proposing 2/25 or 2/26.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-scope-outline.pdf, redwood-cost-model.csv

From: Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@pivotalpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pivotalpay.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & pilot framing

Rafael — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with my notes. A couple clarifications:
- For the interactive flows we care about p95 at the endpoint surface; for the nightly re-rank we care mostly about aggregate $/op.
- Nightly re-rank batches skew larger (typically 32–128), but memory spikes have caused retries in the past. We'll send a small sample of batch histograms for the past 30 days.

We're open to trying quantized variants as long as we can gate quality with your regression checks. Will confirm which re-rank to prioritize — leaning toward the nightly job for the pilot (we can run a smaller interactive subset if helpful).

I can try to get procurement/PO context by early next week.

— Alexis
Director, Platform ML | PivotalPay
alexis.turner@pivotalpay.com

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pivotalpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@pivotalpay.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & pilot framing

Rafael / Alexis — quick add from procurement/ops side:
- We'll need SOC 2 Type II evidence or a SOC2 summary for our security checklist; is there a public summary you can share?
- Procurement timeline: if the pilot requires a paid commitment (small door-opener order), expect 2–3 weeks for our legal + finance review.
- Pricing: can you send a ballpark pilot estimate (not a contract) — just enough for our finance team to greenlight a small trial.

Also, for the nightly re-rank, acceptance criteria for the pilot: overall $/job reduction >= 25% and no more than 1% quality regression on our evaluation metric.

Thanks — Samir
Head of Infrastructure | PivotalPay
samir.patel@pivotalpay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pivotalpay.com>, Alexis Turner <alexis.turner@pivotalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & pilot framing

Samir / Alexis — thanks for the notes. Short answers and proposed next steps below.

SOC2: attaching a concise SOC2 summary (soc2-summary.pdf). For more detail we can send our auditor report under an NDA — please let me know if you want that path.

Pilot pricing ballpark: for the six-week pilot we typically do a nominal usage-based engagement — estimate $12k–18k depending on baseline token volumes and whether you opt into dedicated capacity for the nightly run. I'll map this precisely once we have the sample volumes.

Quantization: we can run int8 variants first and promote lower-bit options (4-bit) only after passing your regression thresholds. We'll bake a regression-suite run into week 4.

Scheduling: Marissa (cc) is our solutions engineer who will lead the technical runbook. Marissa — are you available for a 60-minute technical deep-dive on Thu 2/25 at 11am PT or Fri 2/26 at 10am PT?

Action items (updated):
- Rafael: send pilot SOW + ballpark pricing table once we receive sample volumes (by EOD Tue 2/23) — attached SOW draft.
- Alexis: share batch histogram sample and confirm prioritized re-rank job by Tue 2/23.
- Samir: confirm procurement review point-of-contact if the pilot estimate is acceptable.
- Marissa: confirm availability for technical deep-dive and prepare checklist for data access and redaction requirements.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: soc2-summary.pdf, pilot-sow-draft.docx
